requirements.requirement: The dataops identity exists on both nodes with UID 4500 and GID 4500.
requirements.summary: Both nodes directly report dataops:x:4500:4500 for the passwd entry and dataops group 4500; the same identities remain present after the node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Node1 exports /srv/nfs/shared, owned by dataops:dataops with mode 2770.
requirements.summary: The NFS service is active and enabled, exportfs shows /srv/nfs/shared exported read-write to node2, and the directory is directly observed as dataops:dataops, numeric 4500:4500, mode 2770, including after restart.
findmnt directly shows the expected read-write NFSv4.1 mount at /mnt/shared. The fstab entry and successful automatic recovery after node2 restarted also demonstrate persistence.

requirements.requirement: Files created through either system retain consistent dataops ownership and permissions.
requirements.summary: Files written as dataops from node1 and node2 were visible from the opposite system with UID/GID 4500:4500 and matching mode 660. Final writes in both directions retained their contents, ownership, and permissions after both restarts.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct final-state and bidirectional behavior evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service, mount, identity, data, and write behavior. The fixed lifecycle boot observations independently match the executor's before/after identities. Hygiene is reduced by transient unsigned repository configuration and two retained restart logs, not by functional defects.
limitations: Package-health collection timed out both before and after execution, so dependency consistency and package provenance after using temporary gpgcheck=0 CentOS Vault repositories cannot be independently confirmed (global:before_prepare:node1:package-health, global:before_prepare:node2:package-health, global:after_executor:node1:package-health, global:after_executor:node2:package-health).

operational_hygiene.summary: Task-related package installation, identities, directories, export, firewall rules, mount configuration, test files, and restarts all had clear causal roles. The unnecessary security weakening was setting gpgcheck=0 in temporary CentOS Vault repository definitions on both RHEL nodes; the repository files were subsequently removed, although packages installed while they were active remain. Two minor /tmp/antrieb-reboot.log files also remained after the required restart protocol. No failed services were observed afterward. Other retained test files were bounded functional evidence rather than unrelated experimentation.
